                                  13           Plaintiff previously filed its Motion for Issuance of Letters Rogatory on June 25, 2025.

                                  14   See Dkt. No. 20. The Court found that motion was deficient and (1) failed to ask the Court to take

                                  15   an action and to provide a basis for that action; (2) failed to explain why certain certificates were

                                  16   attached; and (3) failed to attach the related documents for certification. See Dkt. No. 21. The

                                  17   Court denied the motion and gave Plaintiff until August 11, 2025, to renew its motion in

                                  18   compliance with the applicable rules. Id.

                                  19           Plaintiff timely renewed its motion. See Dkt. No. 22 (“Mot.”). Plaintiff requests that the

                                  20   Court sign and seal its Request for International Judicial Assistance. Id. at 1; Dkt. No. 23

                                  21   (Plaintiff’s Request). Plaintiff will then transmit these documents to the U.S. Department of State,

                                  22   which will oversee transmission to Taiwan.1 Mot. at 2. Plaintiff has confirmed it will reimburse

                                  23   this Court, the courts of Taiwan, and the Department of State for any costs incurred and will

                                  24   deposit the necessary check with the Department of State. Id. Plaintiff also attached English and

                                  25   Mandarin copies of the operative complaint and the necessary documents for service. See Dkt.

                                  26
                                  27   1
                                         See U.S. DEPARTMENT OF STATE – BUREAU OF CONSULAR AFFAIRS, Taiwan Judicial Assistance
                                  28   Information, https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/legal/Judicial-Assistance-Country-
                                       Information/Taiwan.html (last visited September 17, 2025).
                                            Case 4:25-cv-02387-HSG             Document 25    Filed 09/17/25      Page 2 of 2




                                   1   No. 23 at 2.

                                   2            “Whether to issue [letters rogatory] is a matter of discretion for the court.” Barnes &

                                   3   Noble, Inc., No. 11-CV-02709-EMC, 2012 WL 1808849, at *2. “[T]he Northern District has

                                   4   previously granted letters rogatory in cases with Taiwanese defendants.” See Chung v. Chih-Mei,

                                   5   No. 22-CV-01983-BLF, 2022 WL 17584243, at *4 (N.D. Cal. Dec. 12, 2022). Plaintiff here has

                                   6   complied with the Court’s directions in refiling its motion, and the Court sees no reason not to

                                   7   exercise its discretion to grant it.

                                   8            Accordingly, the Court GRANTS the motions2 and directs the Clerk to affix the Court’s

                                   9   signature and seal to the forms. Dkt. No. 23. By November 17, 2025, Plaintiff must file a

                                  10   declaration and any supporting proof confirming that the Defendant has been served, or

                                  11   alternatively, a status report (1) detailing where its efforts to serve Defendant stand and (2) how

                                  12   much additional time it needs to serve Defendant.
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13            IT IS SO ORDERED.

                                  14   Dated:     9/17/2025
                                  15                                                     ______________________________________
                                                                                         HAYWOOD S. GILLIAM, JR.
                                  16                                                     United States District Judge

Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13            Plaintiff Robert Bosch Semiconductor LLC filed what it styles as a Motion for Issuance of

                                  14   Letters Rogatory, Dkt. No. 20. The Court finds that Plaintiff’s filing is deficient. Despite being

                                  15   labeled a “motion,” the filing does not actually contain a motion asking the Court to take any

                                  16   action and laying out the basis for the requested action. Plaintiff also includes several

                                  17   exemplification certificates, but does not explain why the certificates were attached, attach any

                                  18   documents for certification, or identify the docket numbers for the documents referenced.

                                  19            Accordingly, the Court DENIES the motion, Dkt. No. 20, without prejudice to refiling if

                                  20   Plaintiff can cure the deficiencies outlined above and otherwise comply with all relevant rules.

                                  21   Any renewed motion for issuance of letters rogatory must be filed by August 11, 2025.

                                  22

                                  23   //

                                  24

                                  25   //

                                  26

                                  27   //

                                  28
                                         Case 4:25-cv-02387-HSG            Document 21         Filed 07/14/25     Page 2 of 2




                                   1            For examples of how parties have submitted such requests in the past, the Court directs

                                   2   counsel to Chung v. Chung Peng Chih-Mei et al, Case No. 22-cv-01983-PCP, Dkt. No. 31, and

                                   3   Fujitsu Limited v. Belkin International, Inc. et al, Case No. 10-cv-03972-LHK, Dkt. No. 119. The

                                   4   Court stresses that it is not its responsibility to help counsel comply with the applicable rules, and

                                   5   directs counsel to do the work necessary to submit a fully legally-sufficient motion and

                                   6   attachments. This includes, for example, determining whether translations need to be submitted

                                   7   with the request.

                                   8
                                   9            IT IS SO ORDERED.

                                  10   Dated:     7/14/2025
